title: PYSEC-2025-19
summary: Affected: PyPI: picklescan picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

title: PYSEC-2024-115
summary: Affected: PyPI: langchain-community A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

title: DHI-sgf4-bliq-423h-4t54 — OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From version 1.0.0-RC1 until version 1.47.0, baggage.Parse…
summary: Affected: Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: ansible-operator-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: ansible-operator-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: ansible-operator-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: ansible-operator-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: ansible-operator-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: ansible-operator-fips and 6772 more OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From version 1.0.0-RC1 until version 1.47.0, baggage.Parse and propagation.Baggage.Extract eagerly materialize every W3C baggage property through parseMember, grow property slices, serialize members, and copy properties into internal/baggage.Item. A valid densely populated baggage header can therefore cause allocation traffic and retained memory disproportionate to its bounded input size. Remote impact requires baggage extraction to be enabled, attacker-controlled input to reach it, and extraction to run before authentication or on a public route; the evidence establishes increased allocation and garbage-collection pressure but not reliable process termination. This issue is fixed in version 1.47.0.

title: DHI-flgv-fsv7-j6m2-6w64 — In `url` 2.5.8 and earlier, `Url::origin()` handled a `blob:` URL by parsing its path as another URL and calling itself…
summary: Affected: Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: amazon-efs-utils-3-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: amazon-efs-utils-3-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: amazon-efs-utils-3, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: amazon-efs-utils-3, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: build-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: build-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: build-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: build-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: build-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: build-fips and 92 more In `url` 2.5.8 and earlier, `Url::origin()` handled a `blob:` URL by parsing its path as another URL and calling itself on the result. It did so regardless of the inner URL's scheme, `blob` included. Each `blob:` prefix cost one stack frame, with no limit on nesting depth. `Url::parse()` accepts a URL with 10,000 `blob:` prefixes followed by `https://example.com/` (50,020 bytes in total); calling `Url::origin()` on it overflowed the default 2 MiB stack of a spawned thread. A stack overflow aborts the whole process, and `catch_unwind()` does not catch it. One such URL crashes any program that calls `Url::origin()` on untrusted input. `url::quirks::origin()` also calls `Url::origin()`. For example, Servo's `URL.origin` DOM getter calls `url::quirks::origin()`, so a script on a page can trigger the overflow. `url` 2.5.9 follows the URL Standard: `Url::origin()` takes the origin of the inner URL only when its scheme is `http`, `https`, or `file`, returns an opaque origin otherwise, and never calls itself. A `blob:` URL with another inner scheme that previously produced a tuple origin, such as `blob:ws://...` or `blob:blob:https://...`, now returns an opaque origin.

title: DHI-goa7-xzav-6j2h-sdkn — OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From SDK version 1.33.0, SDK log version 0.9.0, and trace…
summary: Affected: Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: alertmanager-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: alertmanager-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager-fips-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: alertmanager-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager-fips, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: alertmanager, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: alertmanager, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.23: ansible-operator-dev, Docker Hardened Images:Alpine:3.24: ansible-operator-dev and 6774 more OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From SDK version 1.33.0, SDK log version 0.9.0, and trace version 1.35.0 until version 1.47.0, the AttributeValueLengthLimit and WithAttributeValueLengthLimit truncation paths in sdk/internal/attrnorm, sdk/log/internal/attrnorm, and trace/auto.go do not count valid U+FFFD replacement characters. This is a distinct incomplete-fix defect in the replacement truncation code introduced by the remediation for CVE-2026-81869. Values composed of or dominated by those characters can therefore exceed the configured character and memory bound in span, log-record, and auto-instrumentation trace attributes. Attacker-controlled telemetry attributes can increase retained memory and pipeline pressure, while confidentiality and integrity are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.47.0.

title: CVE-2024-7885 — Undertow: improper state management in proxy protocol parsing causes information leakage
summary: Affected: undertow, Red Hat HawtIO 4.0.0 for Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4, Red Hat build of Apache Camel 3.20.7 for Spring Boot, Red Hat build of Apache Camel 4.4.2 for Spring Boot, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7.3 EUS for RHEL 7, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7.4 for RHEL 8, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7.4 for RHEL 9, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7.4 on RHEL 7, Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 8 and 13 more A vulnerability was found in Undertow where the ProxyProtocolReadListener reuses the same StringBuilder instance across multiple requests. This issue occurs when the parseProxyProtocolV1 method processes multiple requests on the same HTTP connection. As a result, different requests may share the same StringBuilder instance, potentially leading to information leakage between requests or responses. In some cases, a value from a previous request or response may be erroneously reused, which could lead to unintended data exposure. This issue primarily results in errors and connection termination but creates a risk of data leakage in multi-request environments.

title: CVE-2026-120353 — Apache Airflow Standard provider, Apache Airflow CNCF Kubernetes provider, Apache Airflow Common SQL provider, Apache A…
summary: Affected: Apache Software Foundation Apache Airflow Standard provider, Apache Software Foundation Apache Airflow CNCF Kubernetes provider, Apache Software Foundation Apache Airflow Common SQL provider, Apache Software Foundation Apache Airflow Common Ai provider The Apache Airflow TaskFlow decorators @task.bash, @task.sql, @task.analytics, @task.kubernetes_cmd and the common.ai decorators (@task.llm, @task.agent, @task.llm_sql, @task.llm_branch, @task.llm_file_analysis, @task.llm_schema_compare) rendered Jinja templates a second time after the task runner had already rendered them, so any value copied into env, op_args, op_kwargs or the returned prompt, command or SQL was evaluated as a template on the worker. An attacker who can only trigger a Dag run (for example a user with trigger permission supplying run conf), or who controls text that a Dag passes into one of these decorators as an argument or prompt (for example a ticket or a downloaded document), could run arbitrary commands on the worker and read connection passwords and Variables, in any deployment that uses an affected decorator in a Dag that passes such input through env, parameters or prompt. Users are recommended to upgrade apache-airflow-providers-standard to 1.22.0, apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes to 11.0.0, apache-airflow-providers-common-sql to 3.0.0 and apache-airflow-providers-common-ai to 1.2.0 or later.
